records.question: Should NTEC capacity change from 60.5 MW to 41.22 MW per turbine?
records.finding: The EPA notice gives 742 MW from eighteen turbines, each driving a 41.22 MW generator. GEM and the EIA table show 60.5 MW for each of 18 generators, which is 1,089 MW.
records.recommendation: Change each single unit GEN1 to GEN12 to 41.2 MW and GEN13-18 to 247.3 MW with Capacity Per Engine 41.2, because the permit gives the generator rating and the manual records electrical nameplate. Keep the unit naming as it is, since all 18 turbines are covered.
records.researcher_notes: Open the saved EPA notice at https://web.archive.org/web/20260421215236/https://www.epa.gov/publicnotices/ntec-energy-generation-plant. In the Proposed Action section, the paragraph that starts 'This draft permit, if finalized, will authorize' says 'new 742-megawatt (MW) natural gas-fired power plant' and 'Each combustion turbine will drive a 41.22-MW electrical generator'. Eighteen times 41.22 is 741.96 MW. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists 60.5 MW nameplate, 37.6 MW summer and 41.4 MW winter for each of GEN1 to GEN18 on the Planned sheet. The 60.5 MW is probably the turbine rating before the generator. The final permit of August 11, 2026 at https://downloads.regulations.gov/EPA-R09-OAR-2024-0028-0155/content.pdf, Table 1 on page 6, gives the same figures: 'Rated Power Output: 41.22 MW Net-Basis' for each General Electric LM-6000 turbine GEN001 to GEN018 and a 'Combined maximum design capacity of 742 MW Net-Basis'.

records.question: Is the final NTEC permit issued on August 11, 2026 the same project as the draft?
records.finding: The EPA actions table at the saved copy lists the NTEC Energy Generation Plant docket EPA-R09-OAR-2024-0028 as Issued on 2026/08/11. No construction start was found.
records.recommendation: Leave the status as pre-construction and add the permit date to Status Detail. Move to construction only when a source reports work under way.
records.researcher_notes: Open https://web.archive.org/web/20261104114042/https://www.epa.gov/caa-permitting/r9-caa-permit-actions and find the row 'NTEC Energy Generation Plant'. The final permit at https://downloads.regulations.gov/EPA-R09-OAR-2024-0028-0155/content.pdf, Table 1 on page 6, keeps eighteen turbines at 41.22 MW each, 742 MW in all. Neither the permit nor any news story found reports construction under way.

records.question: Should this 2023 plan placeholder be cancelled now that the 2026 plan drops it?
records.finding: The 2023 plan at https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2023-irp-final-pdf adds 132 MW in 2037 on PDF page 218, Table 69. The 2026 plan at https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2026-irp_final_report_only_sc-pdf has no gas unit of that size or year and adds only a 172 MW proxy unit in 2029 on PDF page 177.
records.recommendation: Accept the cancelled status and the cancellation year of 2026 for both units of this plant. If you accept it, also remove the start year and the planned retirement year by hand, since a cancelled unit carries neither.
records.researcher_notes: Open https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2026-irp_final_report_only_sc-pdf, PDF page 177, row New Resources Pending Approval, and PDF page 229, the table of resource additions. The queue row IA-PNM-2025-20 for 172 MW of gas at the Reeves substation in 2029 is in the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory queue file at https://emp.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2026-05/LBNL_Ix_Queue_Data_File_thru2025.xlsx. It matches the 172 MW proxy unit, so it should be handled as one new unit with the Reeves plant, not by renaming this record.

records.question: Should this 2,088 MW placeholder become two Texas plants?
records.finding: The Siemens Energy release at https://www.siemens-energy.com/us/en/home/press-releases/Siemens-Energy-to-supply-ten-gas-turbines-to-Xcel-Energy.html and Table 3-2 on PDF pages 47 and 48 of the 2026 plan at https://e360.prc.nm.gov/portal/public/#/public/nm-prc/en/CaseXscreen?screen=external-Case360&caseId=fe3141c2-1770-4ee1-90a7-f9c3a4749200 give Gaines County, Texas at 1,160 MW and Tolk Station, Texas at 928 MW. Together they equal 2,088 MW.
records.recommendation: Send both plants to the Texas scope as two adds, then cancel or remove this New Mexico placeholder. Keep this unit as it is until Texas has them.
records.researcher_notes: The Utility Dive story at https://www.utilitydive.com/news/new-mexico-regulators-approve-spss-9b-gas-heavy-resource-plan/820978 confirms the New Mexico commission approved 2,088 MW of gas on May 7, 2026. The New Mexico case 25-00066-UT is not in the commission's public case index, so I could not read the order itself. Neither plant is in New Mexico, so no New Mexico point or city applies.

records.question: What is the 233 MW planned gas unit on the Sierra Club list?
records.finding: Table 3-3 on PDF page 49 of the 2026 plan at https://e360.prc.nm.gov/portal/public/#/public/nm-prc/en/CaseXscreen?screen=external-Case360&caseId=fe3141c2-1770-4ee1-90a7-f9c3a4749200 lists 'Dispatchable Gas Thermal - Tolk Unit 5' at 232.5 MW in Bailey County, Texas, for December 2029. That matches the 233 MW.
records.recommendation: Give it to the Texas scope as a separate planned unit at Tolk Station. Do not add it to this New Mexico unit.
records.researcher_notes: I did not cite the Sierra Club list. This is the August 2026 gas plant selection the brief asks about. It is in Texas.

records.question: Does any document state Backup Power for this placeholder?
records.finding: I read the Siemens release at https://www.siemens-energy.com/us/en/home/press-releases/Siemens-Energy-to-supply-ten-gas-turbines-to-Xcel-Energy.html, the Utility Dive story at https://www.utilitydive.com/news/new-mexico-regulators-approve-spss-9b-gas-heavy-resource-plan/820978 and the 2026 plan's resource tables. The Siemens release uses the words 'backup energy' for Tolk in a loose grid sense, and calls Gaines County a 'peaker plant'. No document describes an emergency backup role.
records.recommendation: Leave Backup Power at no. Re-check when the Texas scope adds the two plants.
records.researcher_notes: I found no document that states the value either way.

records.question: Can a person open the commission documents for the Hobbs gas turbine in case 25-00066-UT?
records.finding: The commission approved Southwestern Public Service's gas additions on May 7, 2026, but no readable public document I found names the Hobbs turbine, its model or its site. A Utility Dive article from May 2026 at https://www.utilitydive.com/news/new-mexico-regulators-approve-sps-9b-gas-heavy-resource-plan/820978/ says 2,088 MW of gas was approved and does not name Hobbs.
records.recommendation: Leave the unit as announced at 234 MW and 2029. Ask the project manager to open case 25-00066-UT in the commission's PRCe360 system and look for the turbine model and site.
records.researcher_notes:
What I read:
- The saved 2026 resource plan text for Southwestern Public Service (case 25-00076-UT) names the Hobbs Generating Station of 604 MW, a different plant, in its table of existing resources on its resource list, and the ERAS process on its page 51. It does not name a 234 MW unit.
- The independent monitor's final report on the 2025 request for proposals (case 23-00073-UT) discusses ERAS projects in general and gives no site.
- The New Mexico Environment Department permit harvest for this plant only lists the existing Hobbs Generating Station of Lea Power Partners, not a new turbine application.
- A lead site at https://www.infrasure.ai/project/spp-eras-2025-014 lists the entry at 160 MW, which matches the 159.5 MW credited capacity rather than the nameplate.
- Location was not worked because no document gives an address. The point stays approximate at 32.58532, -103.13716.

records.question: Should Westside capacity stay at 63 MW when EIA lists 60 MW?
records.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 lists three generators of 16, 24 and 20 MW, which is 60 MW. GEM has 63 MW, which is six 3 MW engines plus ten 4.5 MW engines. The permit gives engine power only in horsepower.
records.recommendation: Leave 63 MW as is unless a document gives the electrical rating of the generator sets. Ask the PM whether to use the EIA 60 MW.
records.researcher_notes: EIA file: https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx, sheet Planned, plant 70261, rows WS01 16.0, WS02 24.0, WS03 20.0 MW, planned operation March 2027, January 2028 and May 2028. The permit https://cloud.env.nm.gov/resources/_translator.php/NWFjY2UwMjdjMmQwODZiNzdjZjc0OTYzNF8yMzgzOTA~.pdf shows the J620 at 3,713 horsepower and the J624 at 5,771 horsepower in the original table, and 4,581 and 6,161 horsepower in the Statement of Basis at https://cloud.env.nm.gov/resources/_translator.php/ZjIxMzI5OGU3OWMxZTliZGY4YmJlZThmNV8yMzgzODU~.pdf. Neither states electrical MW as a clear figure. I did not find a Jenbacher data sheet in the budget.

records.question: Is Rio Grande unit 7 still due to retire in 2027?
records.finding: The commission's final order of April 4, 2025 allows El Paso Electric to abandon unit 7 and hold it in contingency reserve until it is retired. The EIA table for September 2026 still lists unit 7 as operating with a planned retirement in December 2027.
records.recommendation: Leave the status as operating and the planned retirement as 2027. Ask the project manager whether the unit should be marked mothballed once El Paso Electric reports it in contingency reserve.
records.researcher_notes:
Opened the case notice at https://epelectric.com/el-paso-electric/uploads/notice-for-23-00403-ut.pdf (page 1, paragraph 1, asks to abandon Rio Grande unit 7 and Newman unit 1 by January 1, 2026) and a New Mexico Political Report article at https://nmpoliticalreport.com/2025/03/06/el-paso-electric-wants-to-replace-aging-natural-gas-generation-with-renewables/ (says the commission did not vote and the chairman said it will likely be approved). I could not find the commission's final order; the commission's case guest index did not show the case in the earlier harvest.

Final order:
- Open El Paso Electric's 2025 resource plan at https://www.epelectric.com/files/24-00260-UT-2025-09-02-EPE-Integrated-Resource-Plan-Report.pdf and go to the footnote 11 under Table 34 at the page printed as 114. It says 'Per the Commission's Final Order, EPE may abandon RG7 and Newman 1 according to the plan submitted in its Application' and cites 'Final Order Granting Abandonment, Ordering Paragraph B (Apr. 4, 2025)'.
- The same plan's Table 34 lists Rio Grande 7 with accredited capacity of 0 MW.
- I could not open the order itself because the commission's case pages are drawn by scripts and the order has no address of its own.

records.question: Should the 2026 planned retirement on Rio Grande unit 6 be cleared?
records.finding: Unit 6 is shown as retired in September 2025 by both the EIA table and El Paso Electric's plan, so the 2026 planned retirement no longer applies.
records.recommendation: After the status change to retired is accepted, ask the project manager to clear the Planned retire value of 2026 and set Retired year to 2025.
records.researcher_notes: Sources are the EIA table at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx (Retired sheet, plant 2444, generator 6) and the plan at https://www.epelectric.com/el-paso-electric/uploads/2026_epe_system_expansion_plan_2027-2036.pdf (PDF page 17, note 2).

records.question: What was the 'Rio Grande CT G10' of 87 MW that was terminated?

records.researcher_notes: I checked https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx (all sheets, plant 2444) and https://www.epelectric.com/el-paso-electric/uploads/2026_epe_system_expansion_plan_2027-2036.pdf (PDF page 17). The 87 MW size is close to the 88 MW shown for unit 9 in the plan, so it may be an early name for unit 9. I could not confirm that.

records.question: Should Afton's planned retirement change from 2039 to 2042?

records.question: Is the 172 MW gas request at the Reeves substation a new unit at Reeves?
records.finding: PNM queue request IA-PNM-2025-20 is a 172 MW gas generator with in-service date January 2029 and point of interconnection "Reeves Substation". The 2026 PNM plan carries a 172 MW combustion turbine in 2029 only as a proxy unit with no site named.
records.recommendation: Accept the new unit 4 record in this batch as announced, since one verified queue entry is enough to add. Move it to its own plant if a later PNM filing places the turbine at another site.
records.researcher_notes: Queue row: Berkeley Lab queue file https://emp.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2026-05/LBNL_Ix_Queue_Data_File_thru2025.xlsx, request IA-PNM-2025-20, which I read from the saved harvest and could not run through the verifier. Plan: https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2026-irp_final_report_only_sc-pdf, the table of modeling assumptions, New Resources Pending Approval: "A new 172 MW combustion turbine is included as a proxy unit in 2029 in all portfolios. Actual resource selection will be determined though a 2029-2032 All-Source RFP Supplement". Scenario 12 in the same report removes this unit. A second check of the plan found: The Berkeley Lab queue file lists IA-PNM-2025-20, 172 megawatts of gas at the Reeves Substation for January 2029, and PNM's 2026 plan carries a 172 megawatt proxy turbine in 2029 in every portfolio except Scenario 12. The Reeves plant agent advised holding it because it could not open the queue file. Accept the unit 4 add as announced; if the 2029 to 2032 request for proposals picks another site, move the unit to that site.

records.question: Should the 2028 planned retirement for CTG1 stay, given the approved extension of the Valencia power purchase agreement?
records.finding: PNM's 2023 resource plan says the Valencia power purchase agreement expires in 2028. A PNM press release from 2024 says PNM asked the state commission to extend it for 167 MW through 2039. A TXNM Energy news item says the commission approved an unopposed stipulation on this application on June 26, 2025.
records.recommendation: Remove the planned retirement year of 2028 or change it to 2039, and add a note that the plant is expected to keep operating under the extended agreement. Check the commission order in case 24-00271-UT first.
records.researcher_notes:
Sources:
- PNM 2023 resource plan, https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2023-irp-final-pdf , section 4.1.3, Valencia Energy Facility: 'The PPA expires in 2028.'
- PNM press release, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/pnm-files-application-for-new-resources-in-2028-302314788.html : 'extension of a Valencia Purchase Power Agreement (PPA) for 167 MW through 2039 (current agreement expires in 2028)'.

records.recommendation: Leave Backup Power as no for all five units. No document was found that states it, so the Data Source box stays empty.

records.question: Should Chino Mines CTG9 stay at Backup Power no although EIA lists it as standby?
records.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx, Operating sheet, plant 54667, generators 7 and 9, shows status SB, which EIA defines as available for service but not normally used. records.question: Is the EIP facility YGI Microgrid the same project as this plant?
records.finding: EIP Oil and Gas Watch lists a facility called YGI Microgrid, proposed, 2,462 MW, at https://oilandgaswatch.org/facility/107ebccf-3e9e-48b1-a8d6-d5a09af92d7a. New Mexico air permit 10883 is for the Yucca Growth Infrastructure 'YGI Microgrid' and its draft permit Part A at https://cloud.env.nm.gov/resources/_translator.php/OTRmYzlmMmMwMTljZDUyM2VkM2I5Y2ZkY18yMzYxNzM~.pdf names 2,462 MW of Bloom fuel cells, so the figure matches the fuel cell redesign of Project Jupiter.

records.question: Does the permit show a different size from the 2,210 MW in GEM?
records.finding: The draft permit Part A at https://cloud.env.nm.gov/resources/_translator.php/OTRmYzlmMmMwMTljZDUyM2VkM2I5Y2ZkY18yMzYxNzM~.pdf says a maximum of 2,275 fuel cell clusters with 2,462 MW. GEM's 2,210 MW (1,223 plus 987) comes from the earlier gas turbine applications.
